pr_title: Support antigravity-cli and antigravity2.0 in gh skill
pr_body:
### Description

`gh skill` recognized only one Antigravity surface. This registers `antigravity-cli` and `antigravity2.0` as skill agent hosts across every `gh skill` subcommand, at both project and user scope.

Fixes #13767

### Key Points

Antigravity ships several surfaces that share one project skills dir but read user-scope skills from different dirs. The two new [registry entries](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/8c6bac8c9/internal/skills/registry/registry.go#L91-L104) map each surface to its documented path:

```go
// Both share the .agents/skills project dir; user dirs differ per surface.
UserDir: ".gemini/antigravity-cli/skills" // antigravity-cli
UserDir: ".gemini/config/skills"          // antigravity2.0
```

Because both reuse `.agents/skills` for the project dir, selecting them next to other `.agents/skills` agents still writes each skill once. Nothing else needs wiring: `--agent`, `--scope`, `InstallDir`, help text, and enum suggestions all derive from the registry slice.

### Notes for reviewers

Start in the [`registry` package](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/8c6bac8c9/internal/skills/registry/registry.go), where the `AgentHost` entries live. The [registry tests](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/8c6bac8c9/internal/skills/registry/registry_test.go) extend the existing `TestFindByID` and `TestInstallDir` tables with project- and user-scope cases for both agents.

The user-scope paths come from Antigravity's own docs, confirmed by hands-on testing (see Additional Context). `.gemini/config/skills` is the one global dir every surface reads, so `antigravity2.0` uses it; the CLI reads its own `.gemini/antigravity-cli/skills`.

### Additional Context

- [Antigravity skills docs](https://antigravity.google/docs/skills) give the official per-surface skill directories.
- [Where does Antigravity look for Agent Skills?](https://atamel.dev/posts/2026/07-01_where_agy_agent_skills/) verifies by experiment which dir each surface actually reads.
- [Choosing your surface](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/developers-practitioners/choosing-your-surface-antigravity-20-antigravity-cli-antigravity-ide-or-antigravity-sdk) explains the 2.0 / CLI / IDE split.

# Support antigravity-cli and antigravity2.0 in gh skill

### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

Currently, the `gh skill agent list` command only supports the Antigravity IDE. We need to expand the feature set to add support for both `antigravity-cli` and `antigravity2.0`.

Additionally, this support needs to be configurable at both the **user** and **project** levels, rather than just a single global scope.

### Proposed solution

Expand the underlying configuration and detection logic of the `gh skill` feature to recognize and manage skills for `antigravity-cli` and `antigravity2.0`.

Implementing this will benefit CLI users by providing a unified workflow for managing Antigravity skills across different interfaces (IDE and CLI) while offering the flexibility to isolate skill scopes per project or sitewide per user.

### Additional context

Verification links and reference documentation:

* [Antigravity IDE Skills Documentation](https://antigravity.google/docs/ide/skills)
* [Antigravity CLI Plugins & Agent Skills](https://antigravity.google/docs/cli/plugins#agent-skills)
* [Where Antigravity Skills Live](https://antigravity.google/docs/skills#where-skills-live)

This request builds upon the existing architecture outlined in the [gh skill install manual](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_skill_install).
